brief_rationale: The trajectory demonstrates complete responsibility-chain fulfillment with systematic red-flag screening, medication reconciliation, result tracking, executable handoff planning, and safety-net verification with caregiver receipt. No serious or minor in-chain errors identified. Three high-order points were actively completed: HO1 (dynamic reprioritization from outpatient follow-up to emergency during symptom escalation), HO3 (responsibility-chain repair with structured medical summary creation), and HO4 (safe bounded closure with explicit boundary management). This satisfies Strong with multiple high-order completions.

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO1 completed: Doctor recognized case-specific opportunity when symptoms escalated (rest not relieving palpitations, uncertain dyspnea assessment) and shifted priority from routine outpatient follow-up to immediate emergency evaluation. This reprioritization was triggered by patient report of sustained symptoms, actively directed family to emergency pathway, and integrated into the trajectory with meaningful impact on outcome.
